newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom to show first MFS benefits.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom to show first MFS benefits.

text.p: Long distance telephone company WorldCom Inc will on Thursday show the first benefits of its ownership of MFS Communications and Internet firm UUNet when it releases its fourth quarter 1996 results.

"WorldCom has a long history of delivering or bettering expectations. It would be particularly impressive this quarter, given so many rivals have been experiencing difficulties," said analyst Bill Deatherage of Bear Stearns.
The fourth quarter earnings per share analyst consensus is $0.27 according to First Call, up from $0.20 a year ago.
WorldCom, the fourth largest U.S. long distance company, acquired MFS in a $14 billion stock swap in August, just two weeks after MFS had finalised its $2 billion buy of UUNet.
Now the three companies offer a complete suite of business services from local to long distance and wireless, coupled with a strong Internet customer base.
"WorldCom has had a wonderful record in integrating companies," said Linda Meltzer of UBS Securities.
She expects the company to reap $350 million of savings in the first year and $800 million in total, with 30 percent revenue growth.
"They will start hitting their stride for cost savings in the second half of the year," She said.
One of the key areas for investors to look at is how well MFS, a provider of local calling and data services to business did on its own business plan.
"People will look at how closely MFS met its break-even cash flow target on a run rate basis," Meltzer said.
WorldCom shares have trailed the broad market in the first month this year after outperforming last year. They closed on Tuesday at $26-5/8, up 1/4.
Meltzer said she has a price target of $32-$43 for WorldCom stock over a 12-24 month period. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
